transcript.content:
You write Verilog practice problems for complete beginners and verify nothing yourself:
your output is checked by a simulator and by mutation testing, and any failure comes back to you.

Reply with ONE JSON object in a ```json code block and nothing else. Keys:
  "spec": plain-English problem statement, 50-150 words. Say what top_module must do and what
          each provided module does. Do NOT give the wiring: which bits go to which instance, what
          a carry-in or select is tied to, or how outputs are combined. Working that out is the
          exercise; the hints reveal it step by step. Never include code.
  "given_sv": Verilog source of every provided module, or "" if none.
  "ref_sv": "module RefModule(...)" with exactly the same ports as top_module, written
            behaviourally (for example with + and assign), never using the provided modules.
  "solution_sv": what a good learner submits: "module top_module(...)" built the intended way
                 (instantiating the provided modules), plus any module the learner must write.
  "directed": list of input assignments as integers, e.g. [{"a": 5, "b": 3}]. Cover the cases
              that expose the common mistakes (carries, sign bits, each select value).
  "hints": {"L0": one sentence naming the concept to think about,
            "L3": the wiring in words (which signals connect where), still no code}.
  "common_mistakes": 2-4 short descriptions of mistakes beginners make on this problem.

Rules: Verilog-2005 (logic is allowed). No system tasks ($display etc.), no `include, no initial
blocks in ref_sv or solution_sv. Clocked logic uses posedge clk. Port names and widths must match
the given top_module header exactly.

Problem id: module_pos
Outline: Instantiate mod_a and connect its ports by position: out1, out2, then a, b, c, d.
top_module header: module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2);
Provided module(s): module mod_a(output, output, input, input, input, input)
Provided module behaviour: Every input must affect the outputs differently so any misordered connection is caught.
The solution must instantiate: 1 x mod_a

{
  "spec": "Design a top_module that instantiates the provided mod_a module and connects its six ports strictly by position. The mod_a module has two outputs followed by four inputs. The top_module has four inputs (a, b, c, d) and two outputs (out1, out2). The first two ports of mod_a are outputs and must be wired to out1 and out2 respectively; the next four ports are inputs and must be wired to a, b, c, d in that order. The provided mod_a is sensitive to port ordering: each input influences the two outputs in a unique way so that any misconnection changes the output pattern.",
  "given_sv": "module mod_a(output out1, output out2, input in1, input in2, input in3, input in4);\n  assign out1 = in1 & ~in2;\n  assign out2 = in3 & ~in4;\nendmodule",
  "ref_sv": "module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2);\n  assign out1 = a & ~b;\n  assign out2 = c & ~d;\nendmodule",
  "solution_sv": "module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2);\n  mod_a u_mod_a (out1, out2, a, b, c, d);\nendmodule",
  "directed": [
    {"a": 1, "b": 0, "c": 0, "d": 0},
    {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": 0, "d": 0},
    {"a": 0, "b": 0, "c": 1, "d": 0},
    {"a": 0, "b": 0, "c": 0, "d": 1},
    {"a": 1, "b": 1, "c": 1, "d": 1},
    {"a": 1, "b": 0, "c": 1, "d": 0}
  ],
  "hints": {
    "L0": "Think about positional port mapping: the order of ports in the module declaration determines the connection when instantiating by position.",
    "L3": "Instantiate mod_a inside top_module and list the six signals in exactly this order: out1, out2, a, b, c, d. The first two are outputs of mod_a and become top_module's outputs; the last four are inputs of mod_a and come from top_module's inputs."
  },
  "common_mistakes": [
    "Reversing the two outputs (connecting out2 to first output port and out1 to second).",
    "Swapping any of the four inputs (e.g., connecting b to the third port and a to the fourth).",
    "Using named port mapping (e.g., .out1(out1)) instead of positional mapping, which defeats the exercise.",
    "Forgetting to declare the mod_a instance or miscounting the number of ports."
  ]
}
